computer-use.content: Computer use is available through the optional opencoder-computer CLI. It delegates natural-language tasks to Cua's own autonomous agent and independently configured desktop model. Use it for desktop apps and browsers on a configured remote target. Commands: opencoder-computer doctor --target TARGET; opencoder-computer run --target TARGET --task-file TASK.txt --output-dir RUN_DIR --timeout 600 --max-actions 50; opencoder-computer status --run-dir RUN_DIR; opencoder-computer cancel --run-dir RUN_DIR. Config defaults to ~/.opencoder/computer.json; place --config PATH before the subcommand to override. Write the full task and requested completion checks in a UTF-8 file. Always choose a new output directory. Do not create RUN_DIR before run or put redirected command logs inside it; run creates it and refuses an existing directory. Redirect stdout/stderr to sibling files. Invoke run as a foreground bash command; do not use nohup, setsid, or shell &. If bash reports an automatic background handoff, retain that process handle and poll status instead of rerunning the task. stdout is one compact JSON object; result_file points to the full result, events_file to JSONL events, and screenshots_dir to numbered PNG files. If the caller provides an image-viewing tool, inspect an actual screenshot with it. Otherwise return the screenshot paths for review; never claim visual verification from a file listing or model summary alone. completed means Cua returned a final assistant result; inspect its summary and screenshots to determine whether the user's requested outcome was achieved. doctor checks desktop connectivity and model-loop selection. Add --check-model --timeout 120 for a read-only model API, native function format and coordinate check; this calls the model but executes no desktop actions. cancelled, timed_out, action_limit, failed, and interrupted are not success. cancel_requested only acknowledges a request: poll until terminal. Cancellation stops future CLI actions but cannot undo an action already delivered to the desktop. Do not issue concurrent runs against the same desktop. If dependencies, desktop permissions, or native capabilities are unavailable, report the error; platform support follows Cua and no custom Wayland workaround is provided. Never put credentials in tasks or command arguments. Do not print the configuration or secret files.
